text:
Priya: FYI apiserver errors + etcd leader flip just after a large GPU node join in us-west1 at ~14:07 UTC.
Jorge: Saw multiple 503s and higher tail latency. Any peering changes?
Priya: No infra deploys except the autoscaler request to add 30 GPU nodes for a training burst.
SRE-Oncall: grabbing telemetry. apiserver traces show a spike in connection resets from 10.6.0.0/16 (new nodes).
SRE-Oncall: apiserver snippet: 
```
E1014 14:07:18.987 1 wrap.go:45] apihandler error: Post https://etcd-usw1:2379/members: dial tcp 10.8.2.5:2379: connect: connection refused
W1014 14:07:19.123 1 transport.go:200] http2: server: write response: broken pipe
```
InfraBot: [netmon] BGP peer flapped on peer-12 (us-west1-edge) at 14:06:59 UTC, routes withdrawn for ~22s
Liam: Ah — route withdrawal would cause some nodes to egress via different NAT pools -> SNAT mismatch.
Priya: That could produce asymmetric routing and drop the control-plane TCP handshakes.
Jorge: Node conntrack on gpu-17: 
```
$ sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_count = 61234
$ sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 131072
```
SRE-Oncall: SNAT port logs show allocation failures in the primary edge pool between 14:06:50-14:07:20.
Priya: etcd member health shows leader switching: etcd-usw1 -> etcd-usw2 -> etcd-usw1 quickly. Leader election jitter.
Liam: Controller-manager reported lost lease and restarted twice.
Jorge: Was there any sudden increase in kubelet TLS handshakes?
SRE-Oncall: Yes: kubelet client connections increased x10 as kubelets registered and metrics exporters started. Many short-lived connections to apiserver and etcd.
Priya: Immediate mitigations: 1) mark new GPU nodes unschedulable (cordon) to stop churn, 2) add temp SNAT IPs to secondary pool, 3) request peering team to stabilize BGP adjacencies, 4) scale down autoscaler joins.
Liam: Doing cordon/drain now: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-15
kubectl drain gpu-15 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
InfraBot: [runbook] BGP team notified (ticket #NET-4221).
SRE-Oncall: Also increased kubelet metrics scrape interval from 15s->60s for GPU DaemonSet via rollout of metrics-configmap to reduce connection rate.
Jorge: Longer-term: consider node-local egress (SNAT), more resilient BGP policies (graceful withdraw), and staggered join windows for large pool scale-ups.
Priya: We should also add apiserver circuit-breakers: lower max-inflight for unauthenticated requests, and tighten leader-election lease durations to tolerate transient network hiccups.
Liam: Cost/ops note: adding SNAT ips and maintaining larger edge pools will increase monthly egress NAT costs. We'll model with finance.
SRE-Oncall: Observability tasks: collect flow logs for the 2m window around 14:06-14:08, export SNAT allocation histogram, and correlate node join events.
Priya: Action items: 1) cordon/drain new nodes (in progress), 2) temp SNAT IPs added (ops), 3) follow up with BGP team (NET-4221), 4) implement join-stagger canary for next autoscaler run, 5) post-incident doc and cost estimate.
Jorge: After drains, apiserver 5xx dropped to near-zero within 3mins. Monitoring looks stable.
Liam: I'll open a Dedicated GPU reserve proposal to reduce repeat burst joins.
Priya: Thanks all. Keep NET-4221 updated and we'll reconvene after the postmortem. :white_check_mark:
